interest: Shows postwar Taiwan unrest, with un-repatriated Japanese suspected of stirring anti-Nationalist sentiment, tracked via consular card files and Tokyo intelligence.
overview: Despatch No. 15 (1948): Consul Krentz reports un-repatriated Japanese may be stirring anti-Nationalist unrest among disillusioned Taiwanese, asking Tokyo for cross-checking intelligence; Instruction 90 authorizes the request.

subfiles.about: Consul General Kenneth C. Krentz reports suspected Japanese subversive activities in Taiwan and requests intelligence from Tokyo to cross-reference against consular records.
subfiles.from: Kenneth C. Krentz, American Consul General
subfiles.summary: Despatch No. 15: Krentz tells Stuart that evading-repatriation Japanese may be inciting disillusioned Taiwanese, citing a Keelung sighting, and asks Tokyo for data to cross-check consular card files.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 15 from Kenneth C. Krentz to J. Leighton Stuart on Japanese Subversive Activities in Taiwan

subfiles.about: The Department of State approves requesting intelligence from the U.S. Political Adviser in Tokyo concerning Japanese repatriates and Taiwanese residing in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Instruction No. 90: State agrees Tokyo intelligence would help check Japanese subversion suspicions in Taiwan, authorizing Nanking to request data.
subfiles.title: Instruction No. 90 from the Department of State to the American Mission, Nanking, on Investigating Japanese Subversive Activities in Taiwan
subfiles.to: Officer in Charge of the American Mission, Nanking
